correctness.rationale: C: In the infinite integer-line graph of distance <=k, the initial k+1 neighborhood facets have nerve ∂Δ^k because each proper subfamily shares its omitted center and the full intersection is empty. The intersection of each added facet with the previous block is a cone with apex a specific old vertex, so adding successively leaves S^{k-1} homotopy invariant. In the k+2-facet nerve, boundary orientation shows translation by one acts on H_{k-1} with degree (-1)^k. For n>=4k+1 the cyclic reduction preserves length-two neighborhoods; Matsushita Proposition 3.5 (read in original text) yields an actual covering of neighborhood complexes and deck shift t^n. Its Borel model is a sphere mapping torus with degree (-1)^{kn}; Wang exact sequence yields integral groups, with k=2 treated separately. Independent finite face-set/homology-over-F2 computations gave mod2 Betti sequences (1,2,1) for (k,n)=(2,9),(2,10), (1,1,1,1) for (3,13),(3,14), and (1,1,0,1,1) for (4,17), consistent with mapping-torus predictions. These mod2 checks do not by themselves prove torsion; integral torsion comes from the Wang sequence. Five Git SHA trees reconstructed.

value.rationale: V: The uniform structural homotopy classification for all stable powers k>=4 provides arbitrarily high sphere mapping tori and explicit parity-torsion, a natural extension of already studied low-degree neighborhood complexes. This is a motivated general theorem, not an arbitrary finite case or just a new naming for known bundles.

final_claim: For k>=2 and n>=4k+1, the open Lovasz neighborhood complex N(C_n^(k)) has homotopy type of a mapping torus of S^{k-1} monodromy degree (-1)^{kn}; for odd k,n, H_{k-1}=Z/2, and otherwise it has the homotopy groups of S^{k-1}xS^1 (with k=2 the torus). The novel range is k>=4, while k=2,3 are credited to earlier results.
limitations: Cutoff n>=4k+1 sufficient only; homotopy rather than PL homeomorphism of actual finite complex.
Finite mod2 homology does not establish integral Z/2; proof relies on sign plus Wang exact sequence.
